dataset.name: NIH ChestX-ray14
dataset.images: row_id + .png; licensed local image root supplied by operator
dataset.prior_study_patient_overlap: allowed and disclosed; shared-panel model replication, not fresh-patient confirmation
dataset.additional_manifests: CheXpert and COCO ordered manifests must be constructed once using README section 4 and shared before model runs

primary.locus: consumed final visual feature block, before connector
primary.score: max present-candidate logit minus max absent-candidate logit
primary.primary_family: 22 models x 3 datasets x 6 questions x 5 clinical/object contrasts = 1980; separate bootstrap within dataset, shared across models
primary.simultaneous_interval: two-sided max-absolute-centered-Z with fixed per-contrast bootstrap SD

probe.refit: bootstrap training patients with replacement seeds1,2, retain all rows per sampled patient multiplicity; refit train scaler and all6logistic probes with fixed projection; COCO resample images

intervention.random_rng: PCG64; one 119xD standard_normal draw then row normalization; saved vectors authoritative
intervention.sham: after random draw, permute each clinical normal in concept order; save all permutations
intervention.tensor_policy: preserve special tokens and padding; perturb consumed image tokens; record branch selection

templates.IY: Is there {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer yes or no.
templates.WY: Does {image_phrase} show {finding}? Answer yes or no.
templates.IA: Is there {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer A if the finding is present and B if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.
templates.IB: Is there {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer B if the finding is present and A if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.
templates.WA: Does {image_phrase} show {finding}? Answer A if the finding is present and B if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.
templates.WB: Does {image_phrase} show {finding}? Answer B if the finding is present and A if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.

DOSE.cohort: first 200 test rows in cohorts.csv order

LOCUS.locus: connector_output (single consumed image embedding stream; family adaptation recorded)

ALTDIR.directions: 6dom+6pattern+6orth+6resid (24 steered conditions per question; no baseline rows)

direction_families.dom: difference of class means mu_pos - mu_neg in the projected, train-scaled 512-d space (known-label training rows)
direction_families.pattern: Haufe pattern Sigma w, Sigma = covariance of the projected, train-scaled features over all training rows, w = seed-0 logistic normal
direction_families.orth: seed-0 logistic normal with its component in the span of the other five concepts' logistic normals removed (512-d space); fraction of norm removed recorded
direction_families.resid: logistic normal (same C, iterations, seed 0) refitted on features residualised column-wise against the other concepts' binary labels (intercept + labels) on the training rows where the concept's label and every used covariate label are known; covariates are dropped one at a time, worst first, while one has fewer than 5 rows in a class on those rows or the rows fall below 25% of the concept's own known rows (CheXpert); a concept single-class on its usable rows keeps the logistic normal (fallback); resid_covariates_used / resid_rows_used / resid_fallback / resid_retention_fraction and the cosine to the original normal are recorded

ALTDIR.lift: every family is mapped to model space exactly as the logistic normal: v = normalize(P @ (u / max(s, 1e-8)))
ALTDIR.prep: python -m cftransfer.altdir --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/altdir_seed0.npz)
ALTDIR.added: 2026-09-14; not part of the planned campaign total (see total_planned_outcomes.ALTDIR_rows_addendum); enqueued explicitly
ALTDIR.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what altdir: per family W (6x6), within-family O_q with 2,000-draw patient-bootstrap percentile interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, own write minus the strongest logistic competitor from CORE, per-concept cosines

EXTCOMP.directions: one logistic direction per extra dataset label (no baseline rows; CORE baseline reused)
EXTCOMP.support_rule: label kept when the training rows hold >= 100 known positives and >= 100 known negatives

chexpert.Pleural Other: 12 known negatives in the training rows (< 100)

EXTCOMP.fit: as the protocol normals: seed-0 projection P, train-only scaler, LogisticRegression(C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0) on the label's known-label training rows; lifted with normalize(P @ (w / max(s, 1e-8)))
EXTCOMP.prep: python -m cftransfer.extcomp --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/extcomp_seed0.npz with cosines to the six normals and calibration/test AUROC)
EXTCOMP.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what extcomp: W_q,extra per extra direction, extended ownership O^ext_q = W_qq - max over the five protocol competitors and the extras with the 2,000-draw percentile interval, extras beating W_qq, verdict over the extended 6 x (5 + K) max-T family

TOKENW.directions: 6 logistic directions x 2 token-weighting variants = 12 steered conditions per question (no baseline rows; CORE baseline reused)

variants.tokenw: weight_t = T * softmax_t(score_t), score_t = the token's projected, train-scaled feature dotted with the concept's logistic normal (temperature 1); mean weight 1
variants.topq: the top 25% of consumed tokens by score_t (round(0.25 T), at least 1) get weight T/k (= 4), the rest 0; mean weight 1

TOKENW.write: h'_t = h_t + alpha * weight_t * ||h_t|| * v_c per consumed token (hooks.token_weights); same total dose as CORE's uniform write
TOKENW.added: 2026-09-14; addendum, enqueued explicitly; no prep beyond fits/vis.last/seed0.npz
TOKENW.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what tokenw: per variant W (6x6), O_q with percentile interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, own weighted write minus the strongest uniform logistic competitor of CORE

PRECISION.cohort: first 200 test rows in cohorts.csv order
PRECISION.directions: the CORE grid: baseline + 6 clinical + 119 random + question sham = 127 (own baseline per setting)

settings.fp32: model weights and forward in float32; CORE batch composition
settings.batch1: bf16 weights; batch size 1 for every condition, baseline included

PRECISION.runner: python -m cftransfer.runner ... --module PRECISION --numerics fp32|batch1; outcomes carry the setting in the `numerics` column (every other module: bf16-batched)
PRECISION.added: 2026-09-14; addendum, enqueued explicitly as two tasks (PRECISION-fp32, PRECISION-batch1)
PRECISION.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what precision: per setting W and O on the 200 rows against CORE on the same rows, max |dW| over the 6x6 clinical cells, dO per question, agreement of the two point verdicts (own > strongest competitor, own > random p95)

ANSDIR.directions: 6 answer directions a_d + the coordinate-permutation sham of a_q = 7 steered conditions per question (no baseline rows; CORE baseline and random family reused)
ANSDIR.prep: python -m cftransfer.ansdir --model-key K --dataset D --n-train 3000 (GPU, enqueued by enqueue --modules ANSDIR as the module's prep task): clean forwards of the six primary-template questions on the first 3,000 training-cohort rows in manifest order, fp32 answer margins to outcomes/ANSDIR_prep.parquet; per question a ridge regression of the margin on the projected, train-scaled 512-d features (seed-0 P and scaler; alpha by 5-fold CV over {0.1, 1, 10, 100}), lifted with normalize(P @ (w / max(s, 1e-8))) to a_q; fits/vis.last/ansdir_seed0.npz holds a_q, the CV R^2, cos(a_q, w_q) and the 6x6 cosine matrix to the logistic normals
ANSDIR.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what ansdir: W^a (6x6), O^a_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, steering reference against the CORE random p95 and the a-sham, own answer write minus the strongest logistic competitor of CORE, cosines / CV R^2

ALTDIRD.directions: 6 dom_disp + 6 pattern_disp = 12 steered conditions per question (no baseline rows; CORE baseline reused)
ALTDIRD.lift: a displacement u in the standardised 512-d space is lifted as its minimum-norm preimage x = R (R^T R)^{-1} diag(s) u (R = the seed-0 projection), unit-normalised; the coefficient lift R diag(1/s) beta of the logistic normals and of the ALTDIR families is unchanged
ALTDIRD.prep: python -m cftransfer.altdir --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; appends dom_disp/pattern_disp vectors, the R^T R / D eigenvalue spectrum and the extended cosine matrices to fits/vis.last/altdir_seed0.npz without changing existing arrays)
ALTDIRD.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what altdird: per family W (6x6), within-family O_q with interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, own write minus the strongest logistic competitor of CORE, cosines to the logistic normal and to the coefficient-lifted dom / pattern

ATTR.questions: 3 attribute questions (view_AP, sex_F, age_60; protocol templates with the attribute phrase) + the 6 clinical questions

attribute_phrases.age_60: a patient aged sixty or older

ATTR.support_rule: >= 100 known training rows per class (both chest sets qualify on all three attributes)
ATTR.directions: 3 attribute directions (fitted like the protocol normals) + 6 clinical normals + the question's sham; attribute questions also score their clean baseline (11 conditions), clinical questions reuse CORE's baseline (10 conditions); no random family (CORE's random p95 is the reference for clinical questions; attribute questions are referenced against their sham only)
ATTR.prep: python -m cftransfer.attr --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/attr_seed0.npz with directions, shams, cosines to the six normals, calibration-row probe and type->random-label control logits)
ATTR.baseline: attribute questions: own; clinical questions: reuse CORE
ATTR.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what attr: 9x9 write matrix (questions x directions), ownership of every question over the family {3 attributes + 6 clinical} with interval and max-T verdict, readability of the attribute probes (calibration rows, selectivity vs the 20 type->random-label controls) and answer AUROC of the clean attribute questions on the test rows

ANSDIRT.directions: baseline + 6 IY-fitted answer directions a_d + the a-sham of q = 8 conditions per (question, template); 40 per question over the five templates
ANSDIRT.prep: fits/vis.last/ansdir_seed0.npz from the ANSDIR prep (python -m cftransfer.ansdir; enqueue emits it)
ANSDIRT.added: 2026-09-15; addendum, enqueued explicitly; INELIGIBLE templates are dropped as in PROMPT
ANSDIRT.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what ansdirt: per template W^a (6x6), O^a_q with interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, the a-sham reference, the cross comparison against the logistic competitors and random p95 of PROMPT under the same template (its two designated concepts), and transfer counts of the IY-owned a_q cells (from --what ansdir) that stay owned under each template

VALID.directions: baseline+6clinical+119random+question_sham (the CORE grid with the block's seed-0 directions; no new fit)
VALID.rows: 200: one frontal per patient of the official CheXpert validation split (200 patients, 202 frontals), selected and ordered by the CheXpert Plus hash rules (manifests.build_chexpert_valid); labels are the radiologist consensus of CheXpert-v1.0 valid.csv (manifests/release.json `valid`, label_source radiologist), not the labeler output of the other roles
VALID.added: 2026-09-15; addendum, enqueued explicitly; images PNG/valid/* of the CheXpert Plus zips (scripts/mayo/extract_chexpert_valid.py); enqueue also emits a features task for the valid rows (features/valid/<locus>.npz) that the module task does not wait for
VALID.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what valid: the CORE grade on the valid rows (W_qq, strongest competitor, O_q with interval, 6x5 max-T verdict from 2,000 paired draws at n = 200, random p95 / |sham| reference on those rows), answer capability of the clean answers against the radiologist labels (campaign rule), probe readability on the valid features against the 20 control probes when extracted, and the paired comparison with the block's CORE grade on the 600 labeler-labelled test rows (per-concept readable / answer-capable / owned, O_q on both, counts of agreeing verdicts)

ATTRRAND.questions: the 3 attribute questions of ATTR only (view_AP, sex_F, age_60)
ATTRRAND.directions: the protocol's own 119 random directions (fits/vis.last/seed0.npz random_vectors, the PCG64(0) draw CORE scores); no new directions, no baseline rows, no prep of its own
ATTRRAND.rationale: ATTR referenced attribute cells against their sham alone while clinical cells had the 119-random p95, so the attribute-versus-finding ownership comparison used two different steering references; ATTRRAND gives an attribute cell the same random p95 bar as a clinical cell
ATTRRAND.baseline: reuse ATTR (the attribute questions' own clean baseline)
ATTRRAND.analysis: folded into cftransfer.analysis --what attr: each attribute cell gains random_p95 / random_n / rank_in_random_family from this module and records steering_reference_sham_only (the old rule), steering_reference_matched (W_qq > 0, > random p95, > |sham|) and steering_reference_rule, which names the reference the cell used; clinical cells are unchanged

VALIDFIT.cohort: test (the write); the FIT uses the 200 radiologist-labelled `valid` rows
VALIDFIT.directions: 6 expert-label directions (vfit:<concept>); no baseline rows, no random family and no sham of its own -- CORE's baseline, 119-random family and question sham are the references
VALIDFIT.fit: the six concept probes refitted on the known-label `valid` rows (role valid, label_source radiologist) with the protocol's own probe settings: the block's seed-0 projection R and its TRAIN-ONLY scaler mu/s (never refitted on 200 rows), LogisticRegression(C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0), lifted with normalize(R @ (w / max(s, 1e-8))); features from features/valid/<locus>.npz (the VALID feature task)
VALIDFIT.cross_fitting: 5 folds over PATIENTS (KFold shuffled, seed 0, over the sorted unit ids), so every valid row is scored by a direction not fitted on it
VALIDFIT.cpu_report: raw cosine (model space and projected 512-d) and covariance-whitened cosine (<a,b>_Sigma / sqrt(<a,a>_Sigma <b,b>_Sigma), Sigma = covariance of the projected, train-scaled TRAINING features) between each expert-label direction and the corresponding report-label direction; held-out probe AUROC against the expert labels and against the report-derived (labeler) labels of the same rows; the seed-0 report-label direction's AUROC on those rows for reference
VALIDFIT.prep: python -m cftransfer.validfit --model-key K --dataset chexpert  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/validfit_seed0.npz)
VALIDFIT.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what validfit: W^e (6x6), O^e_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval and the 6x5 max-T verdict, CORE's steering reference (W^e_qq > 0, > the 119-random p95, > |sham|), own expert write minus the strongest logistic competitor of CORE, and the prep's cosines / AUROCs per concept

PROJSEED.directions: per projection seed: 6 refit directions (proj:<concept>) + that projection's own 119 random directions (projrand:###) + the question's sham (projsham:<concept>) = 126 conditions per question and seed; no baseline rows
PROJSEED.fit: R_k = PCG64(k).standard_normal((D, 512)) / sqrt(512) (the protocol's projection construction with the seed replaced); the train-only scaler is recomputed in that projected space; the six probes are refitted on the SAME training rows and known-label masks with the same hyperparameters (C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0); the random family and shams are the same construction re-drawn from PCG64(k) in that projection
PROJSEED.fit_seed_column: the outcomes carry the PROJECTION seed (1 or 2) in the fit_seed column; direction ids are seed-independent
PROJSEED.prep: python -m cftransfer.projseed --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/projseed_seed1.npz and projseed_seed2.npz with the model-space cosines to the seed-0 directions)
PROJSEED.added: 2026-09-16; addendum, enqueued explicitly, ONE SHARD PER PROJECTION SEED (runner --fit-seed); intended for a handful of representative blocks, not the whole grid
PROJSEED.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what projseed: per seed W^k (6x6), O^k_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval and the 6x5 max-T verdict, that projection's OWN random p95 and sham as the steering reference, the model-space cosine to the seed-0 direction, and the count of verdicts / ownership decisions that agree with the block's CORE grade on the same rows

numerics.weights: BF16 primary; record exceptions as separate condition

activation_storage.required: pooled unprojected features, float16 or float32, all train/calibration/test rows; row ids and masks metadata
activation_storage.optional: full token tensors for 16 preflight images only

total_planned_outcomes.excludes: feature extraction, interface preflight and retries
total_planned_outcomes.ALTDIR_note: addenda rows (ALTDIR, EXTCOMP, TOKENW, PRECISION, ANSDIR, ALTDIRD, ATTR, ANSDIRT, VALID, ATTRRAND, VALIDFIT, PROJSEED) are outside all_test_and_calibration_rows, which keeps the planned total of the original seven modules

addenda_notes.PROJSEED: 907,200 rows per block (453,600 per projection seed). The addenda table states the whole-grid figure by its own convention (per model over all datasets x 22 models); the module is intended for a handful of representative blocks, not the whole grid.
addenda_notes.ATTRRAND: 214,200 rows per chest block (NIH + CheXpert x 22 models)
